To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

disturbed regulation of the serpinB9 gene in circulating T cells of organ transplant recipients is associated with an elevated risk for the development of post‐transplant squamous cell carcinoma of the skin.

DNA methylation of the gene encoding the serine protease inhibitor SERPINB9 is higher in circulating T cells of patients with cutaneous squamous cell cancer (cSCC), a common complication after organ transplantation.
the DNA methylation of the SERPINB9 gene is associated with an increase of post‐transplant cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a novel risk factor in the development of post‐transplant cancer, which may contribute to the identification of new targets for prevention or treatment of this serious post‐transplant complication.
the identification of novel risk factors that can be used for the early risk assessment of post‐transplant malignancies.
the role of serpinB8/9 in T‐cell biology and the development of cSCC in organ transplant recipients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the disrupted regulation of serpin B9 in circulating T lymphocytes represents an early risk factor for the development of post‐transplantation cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas.
the disturbed regulation of serpineB9 in circulating CD8+ T cells is associated to the increased risk for post-transplant skin cancer.

this study provides the first evidence for a role of circulating T cells in the development of cSCC in solid organ transplant recipients and identifies serpinB9 as a potential novel biomarker for the development of cScc in kidney transplant recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

disturbed regulation of SERPINB in circulating T cells, which are involved in the regulation of immune responses, represents a novel risk for the development of post‐transplant cutaneous squamous cell cancer.
disturbed regulation of SERPINB 9 in circulating T‐cells represents a novel risk for post‐ transplant cSCC in renal transplant recipients.
the risk for post‐ transplant cSCC development is associated with a disturbed regulation of serpib9 expression in circulating T cells, resulting in an increased serpinB9 expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of serpin B9 in circulating T‐cells can be used for the early detection of cSCC in organ transplant recipients.
DNA methylation analysis of peripheral blood cells can be used to identify patients at increased risk of developing post‐transplant cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas.
DNA methylation in circulating T cells can be used to identify patients at risk for cSCC.
